items.caption:
Save this one pan lasagne recipe 😍 cannot believe how easy it is and hardly any clean up afterwards! 🙌🏼 cosy season is coming! ❤️

Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil
1 onion, finely diced
2 tsp minced garlic
500g lean beef mince
750g Mutti pasta sauce
475ml chicken stock, plus extra if needed
120g ricotta cheese
Salt and pepper, to taste
Italian herbs, to taste
170g lasagne sheets
120g grated mozzarella
Fresh basil and Parmesan, to serve

Method:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it starts to soften.
2. Add the garlic, season with salt and pepper and cook for another couple of minutes.
3. Turn the heat up and add the beef mince. Break it up as it cooks and fry for around 5 minutes until nicely browned.
4. Stir in the Mutti pasta sauce, chicken stock, ricotta and Italian herbs. Season again if needed and let everything simmer together for about 5 minutes.
5. Break the lasagne sheets into smaller pieces and add them straight into the pan. Use tongs to gently push the pasta down into the sauce, spreading the pieces around as evenly as you can. It does not need to be perfect.
6. Put the lid on, turn the heat right down and cook according to the instructions on your lasagne packet. Mine took around 20 minutes. Check it occasionally to make sure nothing is sticking and add a splash more stock if the sauce starts to get too thick.
7. Once the pasta is tender, test it with a fork. It should be soft and easy to pierce.
8. Sprinkle the mozzarella over the top, cover the pan again and leave for a few minutes until the cheese has melted. If your pan is oven safe, you can instead place it under the grill for around 5 minutes until golden and bubbling.
9. Finish with fresh basil and Parmesan and serve straight from the pan.
.
Recipe adapted slightly from @noaawilliams as I didn’t have any cottage cheese but will be making again with it to see the difference! 😍
.

Another job we’ve been putting off… and once again, it took nowhere near as long as my brain had convinced me it would 😂

This one was requested by you guys for the procrastination series, so of course I had to time it ⏱️

Here’s what I did:

1. Removed the shelves, filter and spray arms 
2. Took apart the filter and soaked it with the spray arms in hot soapy water 
3. Cleaned the walls, base, around the door and inside the edges.
4. Cleaned the seals, although I didn’t take them off because I’ve never been brave enough 😂
5. Gave everything soaking a scrub and put it all back together.
6. Top up salt and rinse aid
7. Run a cycle with a dishwasher cleaner

And that’s it! ✨

Has anyone actually taken their dishwasher seals off? Is it easy to get them back on?!

What job should I time next? 👀

items.caption:
When’s the last time you deep cleaned your washing machine? 👀

I had requests to add this one into the procrastination series and it was another job I’d been putting off, so naturally I had to time it and see how long it actually takes ⏱️ 

Here’s how I deep cleaned mine:

✨1.  Clean the filter
Check your machine’s instructions for where the filter is, then open it carefully and remove any debris. Have a towel or shallow container ready as water may come out.

🧼 2. Clean the detergent drawer
Remove the drawer and give it a thorough scrub, paying particular attention to any build-up around the compartments. I just used washing up liquid for mine as I didn’t have much build up but to tackle mould you could use white vinegar or something stronger like astonish mould and mildew spray. 

🫧 3. Clean the drum and door seal
Scrub the drum. Washing up liquid will be fine for this. Then, pull back the rubber seal and remove any hair, fluff or grime that’s collected inside. Wipe all the way around the seal. Again if mould has built up here, astonish mould and mildew spray is a good option. 

🔥 4. Run a hot maintenance wash
Add your washing-machine cleaner (or whatever your machine manufacturer recommends) I didn’t have one so I used soda crystals, and run the hottest/appropriate cleaning cycle for your machine.

🌬️ 5. Let it dry
Once it’s finished, leave the door and detergent drawer open so everything can properly air out.

And that’s it. Another job we’d built up in our heads that only took 14 minutes and 11 seconds.

What other jobs do you want me to stop procrastinating and actually time? 😂
.
